title: Surówka z kapusty
subtitle: Polish white cabbage coleslaw
excerpt: Finely shredded white cabbage dressed with a light sweet-sour vinegar and oil dressing. The ubiquitous Polish side salad, eaten alongside almost everything, especially fried pork dishes and pierogi.
sourceNotes: Surówka z kapusty (literally 'raw salad of cabbage') is one of the most common side dishes in Polish home cooking. It appears in every Polish cookery book as a standard accompaniment.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days; the cabbage softens but the flavour improves.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make at least 30 minutes ahead to allow the cabbage to soften and the dressing to be absorbed.

content.text: Surówka z kapusty is a simple dressed cabbage slaw that is eaten year-round in Poland with almost every main course. The cabbage is shredded finely, salted to draw out some moisture, then dressed with a light sweet-sour vinegar and vegetable oil mixture. Carrot and a little onion are often added. It is crisp and refreshing alongside rich, fried dishes.

items.prepNote: about half a medium head, very finely shredded
for drawing moisture from the cabbage

content.text: Shred the cabbage as finely as possible. Toss with 1 tsp salt in a large bowl and leave for 15 minutes. Squeeze out the excess liquid with your hands. The cabbage will have wilted slightly.
Add the grated carrot and onion if using.
Whisk together the vinegar, sugar, oil, and a grinding of pepper. Pour over the cabbage and toss well.
Leave for at least 30 minutes before serving. Taste and adjust: more vinegar for sharpness, more sugar for sweetness, salt as needed.

items.cause: Not enough liquid squeezed out after salting
items.fix: Squeeze the salted cabbage in handfuls until no more water comes out before dressing.
Add a little more sugar and toss. Taste as you go; the balance should be lightly sweet-sour.

items.cause: Not finely shredded or insufficient resting time
items.fix: Shred as thinly as possible and rest for at least 30 minutes after dressing.
Rinse the sliced onion under cold water before adding, or omit it.

content.text: Surówka (from surowy, meaning 'raw') is the Polish word for any kind of raw salad or slaw, and kapusta means cabbage. White cabbage surówka is the most common version, but surówki can be made from grated beetroot, carrot, celeriac, apple, or combinations of all of them. They are the default side salad of the Polish meal, appearing alongside kotlet schabowy (pork cutlet), bigos (hunter's stew), and pierogi. Simple, cheap, and genuinely refreshing.
